newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-DUTCH KNP BT PROFIT DROPS 67 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DUTCH KNP BT PROFIT DROPS 67 PCT.

text.p: Dutch paper, printing and office machinery group KNP BT posted sharply lower third quarter profits on Thursday but repeated a forecast that overall the second 1996 would show an improvement on the first.

Third quarter net profit from ordinary operations dived 67 percent to 38 million guilders ($22.4 million) from a previous 116 million, dragged down by a seven million guilder operating loss at its majority-owned Austrian paper making unit.
In the third quarter of 1995 the KNP Leykam unit posted operating profits of 108 million guilders.
KNB BT repeated it was still seeking a partner for Leykam but denied it was planning to completely withdraw from paper making, as analysts had expected.

"We still consider paper (production) as part of our core business," financial director Rob Bonnier told Reuters Financial Television. He said KNP BT was looking for a partner which could offer substantial synergy benefits to KNP Leykam.
KNP BT reiterated its forecast that second-half ordinary net profit would be higher than the 101 million guilders of the first half.

"Given that the fourth quarter is seasonally the best for KNP BT, we maintain our earlier forecast that the net result over the second half of the year will be slightly higher than in the first half," the company said in a statement.

Bonnier said the market showed encouraging signs in terms of sales volumes. Selling prices also showed an uptrend but due to uncertainty about raw material prices market players were hesitant to implement further price rises, he said.
KNP BT shares opened down 0.30 cents at 37.70 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange after the results, and hovered around that level for the rest of the day.
Analysts said the figures held no surprises, coming in almost exactly on target.
They had been expecting the company to post a third quarter net from ordinary operations of between 33 million and 45 million guilders, with consensus at 39 million.
"Overall the results were as expected," said Bank Labouchere's Ad van de Laar.
He said KNP Leykam's results were better than he had been forecasting. "Paper prices are recovering a touch," he said.
KNP BT said the majority-owned paper division was still struggling with low margins.
"The sales volumes were good (in the third quarter), but the margins remained at a very low level," it said.
